tagline: One of the state's highest roads, under an older stone wheel.
intro: From the western edge of the Bighorn National Forest east of Lovell, US 14A climbs steep and winding, at grades up to 10 percent, with truck turnouts along the way. It reaches 9,430 feet at a view that looks southwest into the Big Horn Basin, thousands of feet below. Then it crosses the high country past Bald Mountain and along the North Tongue River to Burgess Junction, where it joins US 14.
Above the road, on Medicine Mountain, is a stone wheel that no indigenous people has publicly claimed to have built. The Crow said it was already there when they came.

moments.title: Medicine Wheel
moments.text: Up a short gravel road and a three-mile round-trip walk, a ring of limestone boulders 80 feet across runs 28 spokes to a central cairn, two cairns marking the summer solstice sunrise.

moments.title: Bald Mountain City
moments.text: A pullout marks the site of an 1890s gold camp, where the harsh climate and thin yields shut the mines within a few years and left only place names behind.

moments.title: North Tongue River
moments.text: On the eastern stretch the river spreads into grassy meadows, good water for trout, then cuts through granite in canyons beside the highway.

practical: Closed by snow in winter and early spring, typically from around December 1 to Memorial Day weekend. Grades reach 10 percent.
